question: In Union Budget 2023, a sub-scheme of which of the following Yojanas has been proposed with the investment of ₹6,000 crore to enable activities of fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises?
solution:
The correct answer is __**PM Matsya Sampada Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Union Budget 2023, the government proposed a sub-scheme under PM Matsya Sampada Yojana with an investment of ₹6,000 crore.
 
• This investment aims to support activities related to fishermen, fish vendors, and micro and small enterprises.
 
• The PM Matsya Sampada Yojana focuses on sustainable development of India's fisheries sector.
 
• It seeks to enhance fish production and productivity through modern technology and infrastructure.
 
• The scheme addresses critical gaps in the value chain including infrastructure, modernization, and traceability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)**

 
 
• Launched in May 2020 with a budget allocation of ₹20,050 crore.
 
• Aims to double fish production and export earnings, and generate employment by 2024-25.
 
• Focuses on enhancing fish production, improving infrastructure, and ensuring sustainable fisheries management.
 
• Includes components like fishery development, aquaculture, post-harvest infrastructure, and fish marketing systems.
 
• It is part of the Blue Revolution initiative for the growth and development of the fisheries sector in India.
 
 
 
• **PM Fasal Bima Yojana**
 
 
• Launched in 2016 to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure.
 
• Covers risks like drought, flood, pest attacks, and other natural calamities.
 
• Premium rates are subsidized by the government to make it affordable for farmers.
 
• Ensures rapid claim settlement for farmers to recover losses and continue farming activities.
 
 
 
• **PM Ujjwala Yojana**
 
 
• Launched in 2016 to provide free LPG connections to women from BPL households.
 
• Aims to reduce health hazards associated with cooking using traditional fuels.
 
• Promotes the use of clean energy and improves the quality of life for women and their families.
 
• Over 8 crore LPG connections have been distributed under this scheme.
 
 
 
• **PM Mudra Yojana**
 
 
• Launched in 2015 to provide loans up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• Focuses on promoting entrepreneurship and generating employment.
 
• Offers three types of loans: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).
 
• Helps small businesses and startups to access credit and grow their operations.
